Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Telemetry spike + request for IRP and SOC 2/SIG artifacts

Hi Karthik —

We observed a short-lived telemetry spike from our integration around 08:40 PDT this morning that correlates with a small number of elevated API calls and unusual error-rate patterns. We don’t believe customer data was exposed, but Acme’s compliance team has asked for:

- Redwood’s Incident Response Plan (IRP) summary and escalation contacts
- SOC 2 control mapping for data access / logging controls (most recent)
- SIG/CAIQ responses or a CAIQ snapshot for our vendor risk intake

We have an internal audit window next week and need to onboard the evidence. Can you provide a secure upload channel and a minimal checklist (redaction guidance + what files you need) so we can share logs and a sanitized trace?

I’ve attached a tiny log excerpt (acme_spike_log_excerpt.txt) to show the pattern.

Thanks —
Lydia Park
Head of Security, Acme Payments
security@acmepay.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry spike + request for IRP and SOC 2/SIG artifacts

Lydia — thanks for the heads up and for the log excerpt. Appreciate the quick context.

Short answers up front: yes — we will provide an IRP summary, the current SOC 2 control mapping for the relevant areas, and our SIG/CAIQ snapshot. We can accept sanitized logs via our secure upload.

Immediate next steps I’ll coordinate:
- Marissa will lead evidence intake and redaction guidance.
- Naomi will prepare the SOC 2 control matrix extract for logging, access, and incident detection controls.
- I’ll provide the secure upload options and an example IRP summary.

Secure upload options (pick one):
1) SFTP drop (preferred for larger logs): sftp://upload.redwood-secure.com/acme-payments — we’ll provide a one-time account and strict retention window.
2) Pre-signed S3 link (for single artifacts) — will expire after 72 hours.
3) Encrypted ZIP sent via our transfer portal (link below).

Required artifact checklist (minimal):
- Application logs / telemetry extract (UTC timestamps) — include sample start/end and anonymize PII.
- Authentication audit logs (if related) — user ids may be pseudonymized.
- Any error-trace files (stack traces) with line numbers redacted as appropriate.
- Business-impact statement (1–2 paragraphs) describing what you observed and your initial mitigation.

We’ll provide:
- Redwood IRP summary (one-page) and escalation contacts.
- SOC 2 control matrix extract: soc2_control_matrix.xlsx (redacted to only controls relevant to the incident).
- SIG/CAIQ snapshot: caiq_snapshot.json and a CSV template for any mapping: sig_row_template.csv.
- Redaction guidance doc: redwood_irp_onramp_guide.pdf (attached).

Please do not send raw PII or customer-identifiable payloads without redaction. If you need temporary vaulting of sensitive artifacts, say the word and we’ll enable encrypted vault access.

Target timeline: if you can upload artifacts by EOD Thu (16 Sep) we’ll aim to turn around an initial intake review within 24 hours and provide a draft postmortem outline by Mon (20 Sep). If you need a faster SLA, let us know and I’ll prioritize.

Best —
Karthik
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
